prompt:
Pixel-art sprite sheet: the WALK cycle of the KNIGHT, a slow, heavily armoured warrior behind a huge rune-carved tower shield, for a Doom/Hexen-style first-person game where monsters are drawn as sprites from several camera angles.

REFERENCE IMAGES, in the order attached:
1. The knight's turnaround sheet (front, front three-quarter, side, rear three-quarter, back). It is the character design: a broad humanoid in blackened, angular fantasy plate with spiked pauldrons, a closed HORNED HELM with two glowing pale-blue eyes in its narrow slit, steel tassets over dark chainmail, an all-metal TOWER SHIELD as tall as the knight (riveted rim, a central ridge, columns of carved runes glowing faint pale blue) on its LEFT arm, and a heavy flanged, spiked steel mace in its RIGHT hand. Also the shading style.
2. The knight standing, seen from THIS sheet's camera view. Match its camera angle, the way it faces, its pixel size, outline weight, scale and ground line exactly.

The shield stays on the left arm and the mace in the right hand in every frame. Never swap them, never draw a second shield, a second mace or a third arm. The horns, the glowing eyes and the runes look the same in every frame.

LAYOUT
- One horizontal row of 5 equal cells, read left to right, each cell as wide as reference 2: cell 1 the standing copy, cells 2 to 5 the 4 walk frames.
- Background: flat pure magenta (#FF00FF) everywhere, with no gradient, texture, vignette, glow, cast shadow or floor.
- The cells are separated by thin vertical lines of pure cyan (#00FFFF), each running the full height of the image.
- Cell 1 is a plain copy of reference 2: the knight standing, exactly as tall, in exactly the same pose. It sets the scale for the other frames, which are drawn at the same scale.
- The feet stand on the same ground line in every cell, at the same height as in reference 2. The knight does not hop or float.
- The whole figure, including the horns, the shield and the mace, fits inside each cell with a clear magenta margin. Nothing touches a cell edge or a cyan line, and nothing is cropped.
- No text, labels, numbers, frame borders, speed lines, motion blur, smear trails, sparks, dust, blood or impact effects. Only the knight.
- Crisp pixel art with hard edges and no anti-aliasing against the magenta. No semi-transparent pixels, and no pink or purple glow bleeding into the background.

THE WALK: a slow, heavy, deliberate stride, the weight of the armour in every step. The shield stays held up in front of the body the whole time (it moves only a little with the steps, its bottom edge just off the ground); the mace hangs at the side and swings a little, opposite to the right leg. The body rises a little on the passing frames and sinks on the contact frames; the stride is short.
- Frame 2 (cell 2), LEFT CONTACT: the left foot forward and planted, the right foot back, the legs at their widest.
- Frame 3 (cell 3), PASSING: the right leg swinging forward past the planted left one, knee bent, foot just off the ground; the body at its highest.
- Frame 4 (cell 4), RIGHT CONTACT: the right foot forward and planted, the left foot back, the legs at their widest.
- Frame 5 (cell 5), PASSING: the left leg swinging forward past the planted right one; the body at its highest.
The four frames loop: after frame 5 comes frame 2 again.
VIEW: front three-quarter, as in the second cell of reference 1 and in reference 2. The knight faces IMAGE-LEFT and a little toward the viewer in every cell; keep this angle, it must not turn to face the viewer. The shield is on the near side, its face turned toward image-left and the viewer; the mace arm is on the far side, past the shield's image-left edge.
The angle matters most: copy reference 2's angle exactly in every cell, including cell 1. The body is turned 45 degrees toward image-left, NOT square to the viewer: the helm is seen in three-quarter, its eye slit and face plate turned toward image-left, one horn nearer and larger; the shield's face is seen at an angle, foreshortened, narrower than in a front view, with its thick edge showing; the knight's right side, the mace arm and the spiked pauldron show past the shield's image-left edge, more of the body visible than in a front view. Do not draw a front view.
